Thanks for reaching out, {user.display_name}! A member of our team will be with you shortly.
Please describe your issue in as much detail as you can.

fields.label: Open tickets category
fields.description: Where new tickets are created (the bot needs View Channel, Manage Channels and Manage Roles there). Empty: the bot creates a "Tickets" category when needed.

fields.label: Claimed tickets category
fields.description: Where a claimed ticket moves. Empty: the bot creates "Claimed Tickets" when needed.

fields.label: Closed tickets category
fields.description: Where a closed ticket moves. Empty: the bot creates "Closed Tickets" when needed.

fields.label: Transcript channel
fields.description: Where the HTML transcript is posted when a ticket is deleted (the bot needs Send Messages, Embed Links and Attach Files). Empty: none.

fields.label: Send the transcript to the member
fields.description: Also DM the transcript to the member who opened the ticket.

fields.label: Open tickets per member
fields.description: How many tickets a member can have open on this panel at once.

fields.label: Ticket channel name
fields.description: The name of new ticket channels, e.g. ticket-{number}. {topic} is the option label.

fields.label: Ask for a reason
fields.description: Show a form asking why the member needs help before the ticket opens.

readOnly.label: Status
readOnly.description: Whether the panel message is posted in a channel.

readOnly.label: Active tickets
readOnly.description: Tickets of this panel that are open, claimed or closed.

actions.label: Publish
actions.description: Posts the panel message in a channel, or updates it there. A message in another channel is deleted.

fields.label: Channel
fields.description: A text or announcement channel the bot can post in.

actions.label: Update posted message
actions.description: Applies the saved panel (message, style and options) to the published message again.

automations.label: Automations
automations.description: When → If → Do rules: when something happens (a message, a reaction, a role change, a member joining, a button click…), check your conditions and run actions such as sending a message, giving roles, XP or coins. Shared with /automation in Discord, where you can also export and import them as JSON. The bot's permissions in the channels you pick are checked when it runs; "Check for problems" lists what went wrong.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Used by /automation in Discord. Renaming keeps its buttons working.
fields.patternMessage: Use lowercase letters, numbers, - and _ only (up to 32 characters), e.g. server-rules.

fields.label: Preset
fields.description: Start from a ready-made recipe, or build your own.

options.label: Welcomer
options.description: When a member joins: post a welcome message in a channel, and optionally give a role.

options.label: Starboard
options.description: When a message gets enough reactions with an emoji: repost it in a channel.

options.label: Thread Joiner
options.description: When a thread is created (optionally only in one channel): add a member to it.

options.label: Commands Only
options.description: Keep a channel for commands: delete every message there that does not start with the prefix, except from staff.

fields.label: Channel
fields.description: Welcomer: where the welcome message is posted. Starboard: where popular messages are reposted (both: a text or announcement channel). Thread Joiner: only threads created in this channel (empty: every channel). Commands Only: the text or announcement channel to keep clean (the bot needs Manage Messages there).

fields.label: Welcome message
fields.description: Empty: "Hey {user}, welcome to **{server}**!"

fields.label: Role to give
fields.description: Optional. Below the bot's highest role, without moderator permissions.

fields.label: Emoji
fields.description: Empty: ⭐

fields.label: Member to add
fields.description: Added to every new thread (a person, not a bot).

fields.label: Staff role
fields.description: Optional. Members with it may still talk there, as do the moderator roles; with neither, staff messages are deleted too. The prefix and the moderator roles are read once: after changing them, create it again.

fields.label: When
fields.description: What starts it. Conditions and actions that do not fit the trigger are pointed out when you save.

options.label: Message sent
options.description: A member sends a message (bots and webhooks never trigger automations).

options.label: Message deleted
options.description: A member's message is deleted (deletions by the bot do not count).

options.label: Message edited
options.description: A member edits a message.

options.label: Button clicked
options.description: A member clicks a button that an automation posted.

options.label: Reaction added
options.description: A member reacts to a message.

options.label: Role gained
options.description: A member gets a role.

options.label: Role lost
options.description: A member loses a role.

options.label: Joined voice
options.description: A member joins a voice channel (moving counts as leaving one and joining the other).

options.label: Left voice
options.description: A member leaves a voice channel.

options.label: Thread created
options.description: A member creates a thread.

options.label: Member joined
options.description: A new member joins the server (bots do not count).

fields.label: If
fields.description: Every condition must pass (up to 10).
fields.emptyText: No conditions: it runs every time.

options.label: Channel is one of
options.description: It happened in one of these channels (or in a thread of one). Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Button clicked, Reaction added, Joined voice, Left voice, Thread created.

options.label: Channel is not one of
options.description: It happened outside these channels. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Button clicked, Reaction added, Joined voice, Left voice, Thread created.

options.label: Category is one of
options.description: It happened in a channel of one of these categories. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Button clicked, Reaction added, Joined voice, Left voice, Thread created.

options.label: Category is not one of
options.description: It happened outside these categories. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Button clicked, Reaction added, Joined voice, Left voice, Thread created.

options.label: Message contains words
options.description: The message contains at least one of these words (whole words, any case). Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Message is exactly
options.description: The whole message is one of these texts (any case). Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Message does not contain words
options.description: The message contains none of these words. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Message matches a regex
options.description: The message matches a regular expression. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Has an audio attachment
options.description: The message has an audio file attached. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Has an image attachment
options.description: The message has an image attached. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Has a video attachment
options.description: The message has a video attached. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Has a text-file attachment
options.description: The message has a text file attached (.txt, .md, .log, .csv, .json). Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Reacted with emoji
options.description: The reaction is one of these emojis. Works with: Reaction added.

options.label: Message has at least N reactions
options.description: The message has at least this many reactions. Works with: Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Message is a reply
options.description: The message replies to another message. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Message is not a reply
options.description: The message is not a reply. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Member has any of these roles
options.description: The member has at least one of these roles.

options.label: Member has all of these roles
options.description: The member has every one of these roles.

options.label: Member has none of these roles
options.description: The member has none of these roles.

options.label: Member lacks one of these roles
options.description: The member is missing at least one of these roles.

options.label: Gained one of these roles
options.description: The role the member got is one of these. Works with: Role gained.

options.label: Lost one of these roles
options.description: The role the member lost is one of these. Works with: Role lost.

options.label: User is one of
options.description: The member is one of these people.

options.label: Clicked this button
options.description: The clicked button is one of these automation buttons. Works with: Button clicked.

itemFields.label: Channels
itemFields.description: Threads count as their parent channel.

itemFields.label: Words
itemFields.description: Whole words or phrases, any case.

itemFields.label: Texts
itemFields.description: The whole message must be one of these (any case).

itemFields.label: Regular expression
itemFields.description: Without slashes, e.g. ^hello\b. Up to 200 characters; patterns that could hang (such as (a+)+) are refused.

itemFields.label: Only count this emoji
itemFields.description: Empty: every reaction counts.

itemFields.label: Buttons
itemFields.description: Automation buttons are posted by "Send a message", "Reply" or "Send a message in the thread" actions; each has a number shown on that action.

itemFields.label: Automation
itemFields.description: The name of the automation that posts the button (it may be this one).
itemFields.patternMessage: Type the name of an automation (letters, numbers, - and _).

fields.label: Do
fields.description: Run in order (up to 10).
fields.emptyText: No actions yet. Add at least one before turning it on.

options.label: Create a thread
options.description: Starts a thread on the message, or in a channel you pick.

options.label: Send a message
options.description: Posts a message where it happened or in a channel you pick.

options.label: Reply
options.description: Replies to the message (or to the button click, visible to everyone). Works with: Message sent, Message edited, Reaction added, Button clicked.

options.label: Repost the message
options.description: Copies the message into another channel, once per message. Works with: Message sent, Message deleted, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Pin the message
options.description: Pins the message. Works with: Message sent, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Delete the message
options.description: Deletes the message. Works with: Message sent, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: React with an emoji
options.description: Adds a reaction to the message. Works with: Message sent, Message edited, Reaction added.

options.label: Remove the reaction
options.description: Removes the reaction that triggered it, or one emoji you pick. Works with: Reaction added.

options.label: Give roles
options.description: Gives the member these roles.

options.label: Take roles
options.description: Takes these roles from the member.

options.label: Add members to the thread
options.description: Adds people to the thread (the member who triggered it when empty).

options.label: Send a message in the thread
options.description: Posts a message in the thread.

options.label: Give coins
options.description: Gives the member coins (needs the Economy module).

options.label: Take coins
options.description: Takes coins from the member (needs the Economy module).

options.label: Give XP
options.description: Gives the member XP (needs the Levels module).

options.label: Take XP
options.description: Takes XP from the member (needs the Levels module).

options.label: Send a saved embed
options.description: Posts one of your saved embeds.

itemFields.label: Message
itemFields.description: Up to 2,000 characters. Variables such as {user} and {message.link} are filled in.

itemFields.label: Button
itemFields.description: Optional: one link or automation button under the message.

options.label: Link
options.description: Opens a web page.

options.label: Automation button
options.description: Clicking it runs your "Button clicked" automations.

fields.label: Button number
fields.description: Given when you save (leave it empty for a new button). "Clicked this button" conditions use it.

itemFields.label: Channel
itemFields.description: Empty: the channel where it happened (pick one for triggers that happen outside a channel).

itemFields.label: Thread name
itemFields.description: Up to 100 characters; variables are filled in.

itemFields.label: Start it in
itemFields.description: Empty: a thread on the member's message. Pick a channel to start a new thread there instead.

itemFields.label: Emoji
itemFields.description: "Remove the reaction": empty removes the reaction that triggered it.

itemFields.label: Roles
itemFields.description: Roles below the bot's highest role, without moderator permissions.

itemFields.label: Members to add
itemFields.description: Empty: the member who triggered it.

itemFields.label: Saved embed
itemFields.description: The name of one of your saved embeds (Embed Messages).
itemFields.patternMessage: Type the name of a saved embed (lowercase letters, numbers, - and _).

fields.label: Cooldown per member
fields.description: How long before the same member can trigger it again (0 = no cooldown, up to 7 days).

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Off: it never runs.

actions.label: Check for problems
actions.description: Looks for deleted channels and roles, roles the bot cannot give, missing saved embeds, reward modules that are off, broken button links and the last error the bot ran into.

responses.text:
Moderation & Safety

Keep the server safe with moderation tools, automatic filters, audit logs and member verification.

MdModeration

Ban, kick, timeout and warn with case history and escalation.

On when the bot joins. Turn it off with /module disable moderation. Set it up with /modconfig.

Settings and their defaults
SettingDefaultWhat it does
DM members when punishedOnMembers get a direct message when they are warned, timed out, kicked or banned.
Command visibilityPublicWho sees the confirmation of a moderation command.
  • /banModerators

    Ban a user, optionally for a set time

  • /caseModerators

    View or edit a moderation case, or list or clear a member's infractions.

Commands-only channels and maths in Counting

LOT 2026-10-27

  • New Automations preset Commands Only: /automation create preset:Commands Only channel:#bot-commands deletes every message in that channel that does not start with your custom-command prefix, so only commands are used there. Slash commands keep working, and members with the moderator roles (or the role you pick) can still talk. Also on the dashboard's Automations page.
  • Counting accepts maths: 2+2, (3*4)-1 or 2^3 counts as the number it comes to. Sums that come to a fraction, such as 10/27, are treated as chat and never reset the count.

Go-live posts for the Live Role

LOT 2026-10-21

  • The Live Role can now post in a channel when a member goes live, with a link to their Twitch or YouTube stream. Set it up with /liverole announce channel:#live-now, or on the dashboard; the message can be customised with {url}, {platform}, {title} and {game}, and ping_role pings a role such as @Stream Alerts with each post.

Auto Timestamps and a new site

LOT 2026-10-20

  • A new public site: the landing page opens every module to show its commands and default settings, runs sample commands with the bot's real replies, and lets you try the Levels settings. New /docs and /changelog pages list every module, command and change.
  • New module Auto Timestamps: when a member types a time such as "friday 5pm" or "7pm EST", the bot replies with a Discord timestamp everyone reads in their own timezone. /autotime enable turns it on.
  • Members with no timezone set are told how to pick a timezone role or use /timezone set.
  • The dashboard's Audit Logs page lists every event that gets logged.

Public landing page and legal pages

LOT 2026-10-19

  • The dashboard got a new look, and the bot got a public landing page.
  • Added a privacy policy and terms of service, plus trusted-proxy settings so the dashboard can be served publicly.
  • Dependency security updates (js-yaml, brace-expansion, ip-address).

Honeypot channels

LOT 2026-10-18

  • Automod can now watch honeypot channels: whoever posts in one is softbanned (or banned, kicked or timed out) at once, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts. /automod honeypot add can create the channel and post a warning in it.

More reaction-role templates

LOT 2026-10-17

  • Reaction roles gained ready-made role sets: pronouns, colours, age ranges and more.

Timezones

LOT 2026-10-16

  • Added /timestamp, /timezone and timezone roles, so times show up in each member's own timezone.
  • Timezone reaction-role templates in /reactionrole and the dashboard, and a timezone-roles editor on the dashboard's General page.
  • Custom commands limited to certain roles are now hidden from members who can't run them.

Performance and fixes

LOT 2026-10-15

  • A performance pass across the bot, including buffered achievement message counts.
  • Added /owner, which pings the bot owner.
  • Fixed the bugs found in a full codebase review.

Counting

LOT 2026-10-14

  • New module Counting: members count up from 1 in turns; a wrong number or a double turn starts it over.
  • The bot owner can see who added the bot to each server.

Dashboard access

LOT 2026-10-13

  • The dashboard shows only the servers you manage; the bot owner can manage, and join, any server the bot is in.
  • Translation activity per channel on the dashboard.
  • Setup commands can create the role or channel they ask for.
  • Moderator commands now require default member permissions too.

The web dashboard

LOT 2026-10-11

  • Added the web dashboard: log in with Discord and change every module's settings in a browser.
  • Manage saved embeds, custom commands, reminders, feeds, level rewards, the shop and achievements from it.
  • Run giveaways and polls, build automations, manage reaction-role and ticket panels, and moderate members (XP and coins too) from the dashboard.
  • An embed editor, member pickers and long-list paging.
  • The bot itself was rebuilt for feature parity with MEE6, with the audited bugs fixed.

Docker and CI

LOT 2026-09-27

  • Docker image, health endpoints, CI with GitHub Container Registry publishing, rollback and Dependabot.
  • A LibreTranslate backend for translation, with back-off on rate limits.
  • A failing event handler no longer restarts the bot; a shard that disconnects for good stops it cleanly.

README and license

LOT 2026-08-23

  • Added the README and the MIT license.

First version

LOT 2026-06-11

  • The first version of the bot, including the games command and Scrabble.

Frost.Byte
What's inside Dashboard demo Docs Changelog GitHub Log in
Log in Add to Discord

Frost.Byte 42 modules, one Discord bot. Free, with no premium tier.

Pick the modules your server needs, switch them on with /module, and tune every option from the web dashboard.

FreeAdd to Discord Log in to the dashboard

Try a flavour

  • Net 79 slash commands
  • Contents 42 modules, individually wrapped
  • Free from premium tiers and paid API keys

What's inside: 42 modules, one switch each.

Every feature comes individually wrapped. Open one to see its commands and the settings it ships with; switch it on with /module enable or one click on the dashboard, and whatever you leave off stays out of your way.

Cherry Moderation & Safety

7 modules

Keep the server safe with moderation tools, automatic filters, audit logs and member verification.

  • MdModerationBan, kick, timeout and warn with case history and escalation.On at start

    On when the bot joins. Off: /module disable moderation

    Set it up: /modconfig

    Commands

    • /ban Ban a user, optionally for a set time
    • /case View or edit a moderation case, or list or clear a member's infractions.
    • /kick Kick a member from the server
    • /modconfig Moderator settings: escalation, immune and mod roles, mute role, case log, visibility.
    • /purge Bulk-delete recent messages in this channel
    • /slowmode Set or remove a channel's slowmode
    • /softban Ban and instantly unban a user to delete their recent messages.
    • /timeout Time out a member; over 28 days uses the mute role
    • /unban Lift a ban by user ID
    • /unmute Remove a member's timeout or mute role
    • /warn Warn a member; warnings can trigger automatic actions

    Settings, as they ship

    DM members when punished
    On
    Command visibility
    Public
    Everything in Moderation
  • AmAuto-ModerationAutomatically removes or punishes bad words, spam, invites, links, caps, mass mentions and more.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable automod

    Set it up: /automod

    Commands

    • /automod Auto-moderation rules, actions and exemptions
    Everything in Auto-Moderation
  • LgAudit LogsPosts message, member, voice, channel, role and server events to your log channels.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable logging

    Set it up: /logging

    Commands

    • /logging Audit logs: turn on/off, pick log channels, toggle events
    Everything in Audit Logs
  • CpVerificationNew members solve a captcha before they get access; those who never verify can be kicked.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable captcha

    Set it up: /captcha

    Commands

    • /captcha Captcha verification for new members

    Settings, as they ship

    Captcha type
    Image code
    Kick unverified members after (minutes)
    0
    Everything in Verification
  • ArAnti-RaidSpots join floods and brand-new accounts, pauses invites and alerts your moderators.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable antiraid

    Set it up: /antiraid

    Commands

    • /antiraid Raid protection: join floods, lockdowns and brand-new accounts.

    Settings, as they ship

    Joins
    10
    Window
    10 seconds
    Members who join during a raid
    Only alert the moderators
    Pause invites
    On
    Everything in Anti-Raid
  • RpRole PersistenceGives members their roles and nickname back when they leave and rejoin.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable rolepersist

    Set it up: /rolepersist

    Commands

    • /rolepersist Give members their roles back when they leave and rejoin.

    Settings, as they ship

    Give back nicknames
    On
    Keep for
    90 days
    Everything in Role Persistence
  • BkServer BackupsSaves your roles, channels and permissions, and rebuilds what a raid or a mistake deleted.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable backups

    Set it up: /backup

    Commands

    • /backup Back up and restore roles, channels and permissions.

    Settings, as they ship

    Back up every
    0 hours
    Automatic backups kept
    7
    Everything in Server Backups

Lemon Community

18 modules

Greet members, hand out roles and run the features your community uses every day.

  • WlWelcome & GoodbyeGreets new members with a message, a welcome card or a DM, says goodbye and gives autoroles.Off at start

    Switch it on: /module enable welcome

    Set it up: /welcome

    Commands

    • /welcome Welcome & Goodbye: join message, card, DM, autoroles and goodbye

    Settings, as they ship

    Welcome message in a channel
    On
    Welcome message as an embed
    On
    Message text
    Hey {user}, welcome to **{server}**!
    Welcome DM
    Off
    Everything in Welcome & Goodbye
  • RrReaction RolesMembers pick their own roles from buttons, a dropdown or emoji reactions.On at start

    On when the bot joins. Off: /module disable reactionroles

    Set it up: /reactionrole

    Commands

    • /reactionrole Role panels with buttons, a dropdown or emoji reactions
    Everything in Reaction Roles
  • IvInvite TrackerTracks who invited whom, with an invite leaderboard and personal invite links.On at start

    On when the bot joins. Off: /module disable invites

    Set it up: /invites

    Commands

    • /invites Invite Tracker: /invites, /inviter, /invites-leaderboard and personal links
    Everything in Invite Tracker
  • TkTicketingSupport ticket panels with categories, staff claiming and HTML transcripts.On at start

    On when the bot joins. Off: /module disable tickets

    Set it up: /ticket-panel

    Commands

    • /ticket Manage the ticket in this channel
    • /ticket-panel Set up ticket panels: options, managers, categories, transcripts
    Everything in Ticketing

Getting started

  1. Add Frost.Byte to a server where you have Manage Server: invite the bot. Its slash commands appear on their own.
  2. Switch on the modules you want. Run /module list to see them all and /module enable <name> to turn one on, or flip its switch on the dashboard. A module's setup command works while the module is still off, so you can configure it first.
  3. Fine-tune on the web. Log in to the dashboard with Discord, pick the server, and set channels, roles, messages and limits for each module.
  4. Check what members see. /help lists only the commands that member can run and that are switched on.

Who can run what

Everyone
Any member, in a server where the command's module is on.
Moderators
Members with the moderator permissions the command asks for, or a moderator role set with /modconfig.
Admins
Members with Manage Server. Discord hides these commands from everyone else, and the bot checks again.

Moderation & Safety

Keep the server safe with moderation tools, automatic filters, audit logs and member verification.

MdModeration

Ban, kick, timeout and warn with case history and escalation.

On when the bot joins. Turn it off with /module disable moderation. Set it up with /modconfig.

Settings and their defaults
SettingDefaultWhat it does
DM members when punishedOnMembers get a direct message when they are warned, timed out, kicked or banned.
Command visibilityPublicWho sees the confirmation of a moderation command.
  • /banModerators

    Ban a user, optionally for a set time

  • /caseModerators

    View or edit a moderation case, or list or clear a member's infractions.

    • /case view View a case.
    • /case reason Change a case's reason.
    • /case proof Set a case's proof link.
    • /case history List a member's moderation cases
    • /case clear-history Pardon all of a member's active warnings
  • /kickModerators

    Kick a member from the server

  • /modconfigAdmins

    Moderator settings: escalation, immune and mod roles, mute role, case log, visibility.

    • /modconfig escalation add Add or update a tier: N warnings within a period, then an action.
    • /modconfig escalation remove Remove an escalation tier.
    • /modconfig escalation list List the escalation tiers.
    • /modconfig immune add Make a role immune.
    • /modconfig immune remove Remove a role from the immune list.
    • /modconfig immune list List the immune roles.
    • /modconfig modroles add Give a role moderator access.
    • /modconfig modroles remove Remove a moderator role.
    • /modconfig modroles list List the moderator roles.
    • /modconfig muterole Set, create or clear the mute role (used for mutes over 28 days).
    • /modconfig logchannel Set or clear the channel for moderation case logs.
    • /modconfig visibility Who sees moderation command replies
    • /modconfig dm Turn DMs to punished members on or off.
    • /modconfig show Show the current moderation settings.
  • /purgeModerators

    Bulk-delete recent messages in this channel

  • /slowmodeModerators

    Set or remove a channel's slowmode

  • /softbanModerators

    Ban and instantly unban a user to delete their recent messages.

  • /timeoutModerators

    Time out a member; over 28 days uses the mute role

  • /unbanModerators

    Lift a ban by user ID

  • /unmuteModerators

    Remove a member's timeout or mute role

  • /warnModerators

    Warn a member; warnings can trigger automatic actions

AmAuto-Moderation

Automatically removes or punishes bad words, spam, invites, links, caps, mass mentions and more.

Off until you run /module enable automod or flip its switch on the dashboard. Set it up with /automod.

Configured with its commands and the lists on the dashboard.

  • /automodAdmins

    Auto-moderation rules, actions and exemptions

    • /automod enable Turn automod on. Your rules and lists stay as they are.
    • /automod disable Turn automod off. Rules and lists are kept.
    • /automod status Show every rule with its action and scope, the lists and the exemptions.
    • /automod rule Set a rule's action, threshold and scope (Bad Words, Caps, Anti-Spam, …).
    • /automod words add Add words or phrases (comma-separated).
    • /automod words remove Remove a word or phrase.
    • /automod words list List the filtered words (only you can see the list).
    • /automod patterns add Add a case-insensitive regex pattern.
    • /automod patterns remove Remove a regex pattern.
    • /automod patterns list List the regex patterns (only you can see the list).
    • /automod domains add Add a domain to the blocked or allowed list.
    • /automod domains remove Remove a domain from the blocked and allowed lists.
    • /automod domains list Show the blocked and allowed domains.
    • /automod exempt add Add a role and/or channel to the exemptions or to a rule's list.
    • /automod exempt remove Remove a role and/or channel from the exemptions or a rule's list.
    • /automod honeypot add Make a channel a honeypot, or create one.
    • /automod honeypot remove Stop a channel being a honeypot (the channel is kept).

LgAudit Logs

Posts message, member, voice, channel, role and server events to your log channels.

Off until you run /module enable logging or flip its switch on the dashboard. Set it up with /logging.

Configured with its commands and the lists on the dashboard.

  • /loggingAdmins

    Audit logs: turn on/off, pick log channels, toggle events

    • /logging enable Turn audit logging on.
    • /logging disable Turn audit logging off (settings are kept).
    • /logging status Show log channels, disabled events and ignored channels.
    • /logging channel Set or clear the channel for a log type.
    • /logging event Turn one log event (or all) on or off.
    • /logging ignore add Stop logging message events in a channel or category.
    • /logging ignore remove Log message events in a channel again.
    • /logging ignore list List ignored channels.

CpVerification

New members solve a captcha before they get access; those who never verify can be kicked.

Off until you run /module enable captcha or flip its switch on the dashboard. Set it up with /captcha.

Settings and their defaults
SettingDefaultWhat it does
Captcha typeImage codeImage: type the code from a picture. Button: one click.
Kick unverified members after (minutes)00 never kicks; otherwise 5 to 10080 minutes (7 days). Setting 0 cancels the kicks already scheduled.
  • /captchaAdmins

    Captcha verification for new members

    • /captcha setup Create or reuse #verification and the role, then post the panel.
    • /captcha enable Turn verification on.
    • /captcha disable Turn verification off (settings are kept).
    • /captcha status Show the settings and any problems.
    • /captcha mode Image code or one-click button.
    • /captcha role Set the verified role.
    • /captcha require Roles needed to verify, and a form for those without (no options: show).
    • /captcha channel Move the panel to another channel.
    • /captcha timeout Kick members who do not verify in time.
    • /captcha message Edit the panel (no options opens a form).
    • /captcha lock Hide channels until members verify
    • /captcha verify-existing Give the verified role to current members.

Changelog

What changed in Frost.Byte, newest first. Each entry is dated by when it landed on main; there are no version numbers yet. The full history is in the commit log.

Commands-only channels and maths in Counting

LOT 2026-10-27

  • New Automations preset Commands Only: /automation create preset:Commands Only channel:#bot-commands deletes every message in that channel that does not start with your custom-command prefix, so only commands are used there. Slash commands keep working, and members with the moderator roles (or the role you pick) can still talk. Also on the dashboard's Automations page.
  • Counting accepts maths: 2+2, (3*4)-1 or 2^3 counts as the number it comes to. Sums that come to a fraction, such as 10/27, are treated as chat and never reset the count.

Go-live posts for the Live Role

LOT 2026-10-21

  • The Live Role can now post in a channel when a member goes live, with a link to their Twitch or YouTube stream. Set it up with /liverole announce channel:#live-now, or on the dashboard; the message can be customised with {url}, {platform}, {title} and {game}, and ping_role pings a role such as @Stream Alerts with each post.

Auto Timestamps and a new site

LOT 2026-10-20

  • A new public site: the landing page opens every module to show its commands and default settings, runs sample commands with the bot's real replies, and lets you try the Levels settings. New /docs and /changelog pages list every module, command and change.
  • New module Auto Timestamps: when a member types a time such as "friday 5pm" or "7pm EST", the bot replies with a Discord timestamp everyone reads in their own timezone. /autotime enable turns it on.
  • Members with no timezone set are told how to pick a timezone role or use /timezone set.
  • The dashboard's Audit Logs page lists every event that gets logged.

Public landing page and legal pages

LOT 2026-10-19

  • The dashboard got a new look, and the bot got a public landing page.
  • Added a privacy policy and terms of service, plus trusted-proxy settings so the dashboard can be served publicly.
  • Dependency security updates (js-yaml, brace-expansion, ip-address).

Honeypot channels

LOT 2026-10-18

  • Automod can now watch honeypot channels: whoever posts in one is softbanned (or banned, kicked or timed out) at once, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts. /automod honeypot add can create the channel and post a warning in it.

More reaction-role templates

LOT 2026-10-17

  • Reaction roles gained ready-made role sets: pronouns, colours, age ranges and more.

Timezones

LOT 2026-10-16

  • Added /timestamp, /timezone and timezone roles, so times show up in each member's own timezone.
  • Timezone reaction-role templates in /reactionrole and the dashboard, and a timezone-roles editor on the dashboard's General page.
  • Custom commands limited to certain roles are now hidden from members who can't run them.

Performance and fixes

LOT 2026-10-15

  • A performance pass across the bot, including buffered achievement message counts.
  • Added /owner, which pings the bot owner.
  • Fixed the bugs found in a full codebase review.

Counting

LOT 2026-10-14

  • New module Counting: members count up from 1 in turns; a wrong number or a double turn starts it over.
  • The bot owner can see who added the bot to each server.

Dashboard access

LOT 2026-10-13

  • The dashboard shows only the servers you manage; the bot owner can manage, and join, any server the bot is in.
  • Translation activity per channel on the dashboard.
  • Setup commands can create the role or channel they ask for.
  • Moderator commands now require default member permissions too.

The web dashboard

LOT 2026-10-11

  • Added the web dashboard: log in with Discord and change every module's settings in a browser.
  • Manage saved embeds, custom commands, reminders, feeds, level rewards, the shop and achievements from it.
  • Run giveaways and polls, build automations, manage reaction-role and ticket panels, and moderate members (XP and coins too) from the dashboard.
  • An embed editor, member pickers and long-list paging.
  • The bot itself was rebuilt for feature parity with MEE6, with the audited bugs fixed.

Docker and CI

LOT 2026-09-27

  • Docker image, health endpoints, CI with GitHub Container Registry publishing, rollback and Dependabot.
  • A LibreTranslate backend for translation, with back-off on rate limits.
  • A failing event handler no longer restarts the bot; a shard that disconnects for good stops it cleanly.

README and license

LOT 2026-08-23

  • Added the README and the MIT license.

First version

LOT 2026-06-11

  • The first version of the bot, including the games command and Scrabble.

Something broken? Report it on GitHub.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 19 October 2026

This policy covers the Discord bot and its web dashboard. They are run by one person, the bot owner, not by a company. Questions or requests: the bot owner, through the server where you use the bot.

What the bot stores

The bot keeps only what its features need, in a database on the bot owner's own server:

  • Server settings that server staff choose: which modules are on, channels, roles, messages, embeds, custom commands, automations, panels and similar.
  • Discord IDs of servers, channels, roles, messages and members, so the bot knows where and to whom a feature applies.
  • Feature data about members, only for features a server turns on:
    • levels and XP, message counts and voice minutes
    • economy balances, items and boosts
    • achievements
    • birthdays (day and month, and the year only if you give it)
    • your time zone, if you set one
    • poll votes and giveaway entries
    • who invited whom, and when members joined or left
    • ticket owners and the reason you give when opening a ticket
    • temporary voice channel owners
    • captcha checks (a hashed answer and attempt count, removed when the check ends)
  • Moderation records (warnings, timeouts, kicks and bans) with the moderator, the member and the reason given.
  • Who added the bot to each server, for the bot owner.

The bot reads messages to run its features: commands, auto-moderation, auto-responders, levels, translation, logging, starboards and counting. It does not save message text in its database. When a server turns logging on, edited and deleted messages are posted to that server's own log channel. Ticket transcripts are posted to the server's channel or sent to you by DM, not kept by the bot.

The dashboard

  • You log in with Discord. The dashboard asks Discord only for your profile (ID, username, display name and avatar) and your list of servers with your permissions in them.
  • Your Discord login token is stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser for up to 7 days, not in the bot's database. Logging out ends it at Discord too.
  • The only cookies are that login cookie and a short-lived one used while you log in. There are no ads, analytics or tracking cookies.
  • Logins, logouts and settings changes are written to the dashboard's server log with your Discord user ID.
  • The dashboard is reached through Cloudflare, which carries the connection and sees your IP address.
  • The website and the dashboard load their fonts from Google Fonts, so your browser also connects to Google, which sees your IP address. No cookies are set for this.

Who else sees data

  • Discord, which hosts everything the bot posts.
  • Translation: text you translate, or that is posted in an auto-translate channel, goes to a translation server the bot owner runs (LibreTranslate). Results are cached for up to an hour.
  • Lookup commands send what you type to the site that answers: /search anime and /search manga to AniList, /search pokemon to PokéAPI, and /search urban to Urban Dictionary.
  • Social feeds that staff set up (RSS, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky, podcasts) are fetched from those sites. No member data is sent to them.

Data is never sold or shared for advertising.

How long data is kept

  • Data stays while the bot is in the server. If the bot is removed, its data is kept, so the settings come back if the bot is added again, until someone asks for it to be deleted.
  • Some records are removed automatically when they are no longer needed, for example finished captcha checks and a birthday you remove.
  • Backups are kept for up to six months, then deleted.

Your choices

  • You can ask for a copy of the data the bot holds about you, or for it to be deleted, by contacting the bot owner, through the server where you use the bot. Deleting it resets things like your levels and balances.
